mainTopic: Hair strings and חציצה, and the head ornaments a woman may not wear out on שבת (טוטפת, כבול, איסטמא)
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion of חציצה in טבילה. A wide neck-strap (קטלא) blocks the water because a woman wears it tight on purpose. רבי יהודה says strings of wool and of hair do not block. שמואל first seems to rule like him only on hair, and אביי asks who disagrees about hair at all. A corrected version of שמואל, a ברייתא, and our own משנה all show that the חכמים agree hair strings are not a חציצה. The גמרא then returns to items a woman may not wear out on שבת. The טוטפת is not a protective spice packet, which would be allowed like a proven קמיע. It is a forehead ornament, and רבי אבהו explains how it differs from the סרביטין. The כבול is most likely a woolen cap, and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר teaches that what is worn under the hairnet may be worn outside. Finally the גמרא defines the איסטמא as a small band holding in stray hairs and lists three rules about it. A further statement in רבי שמעון's name begins and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The case is a wide neck-strap that a woman wears tightly on purpose
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the earlier question. The משנה is talking about a קטלא, a wide decorative neck-strap. A woman does tighten it, because she likes to look fuller.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here we are dealing with a קטלא, a wide neck-strap. A woman does tighten it around her own neck, because she likes to look fleshy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its answer to the question on the previous amud: 'Why would a strap around the neck block the water? A woman does not choke herself!' It answers that the case is a special wide strap that a woman does wear tightly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed that nothing on the neck is ever tight, so water would always get under it. The answer names a specific item, the קטלא. It is wide, so tightening it does not hurt, and a woman wants it tight so that flesh shows around it, which was seen as attractive. Since it really is tight, water cannot reach underneath, so it counts as a חציצה.

keyTerms.meaning: Here we are dealing with (narrowing the case)
A wide, decorated strap worn around the neck
Chokes / tightens around the neck
It pleases her / she prefers it
A fleshy, full-figured woman

steps.confusionAlert: 'חונקת את עצמה' does not mean she harms herself. It only means she wears the strap snugly. Because the strap is wide, it is not painful.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that חציצה depends on whether the item is really tight against the body, and that this depends on how people normally wear it.

phrases.english: Here we are dealing with a katla (a wide neck-strap),
phrases.notes: The גמרא is saying the משנה is talking about this one specific item.

phrases.english: which a woman does tighten around her own neck —
phrases.notes: Directly answers the earlier claim that a woman does not choke herself.

phrases.english: because she is pleased to appear fleshy.
phrases.notes: Explains her motive. Flesh pressing out around the strap looked attractive.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised on the previous amud: 'a woman does not choke herself, so why would a neck-strap block the water?'
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא) to a specific item
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have thought nothing around the neck is ever tight, so it could never block the water.
steps.terutzMaskana: A קטלא is deliberately worn tight, so it does block the water and counts as a חציצה.

steps.title: רבי יהודה says wool and hair strings do not block water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא keeps quoting the משנה in מקואות. רבי יהודה rules that strings of wool and of hair are not a חציצה, because water soaks through them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: strings of wool and strings of hair do not block, because the water gets through them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next line of the same משנה in מקואות, which brings רבי יהודה's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part of the משנה said that wool strings, for example, block the water. רבי יהודה disagrees for wool and hair, because these materials are absorbent and let water through. Water reaching the skin is all that טבילה needs, so these strings do not interrupt it.

keyTerms.meaning: Block / interpose (from חציצה), stopping water from reaching the body
Wool
Hair
The water gets into and through them

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets up the principle that a material water can pass through is not a חציצה, even if it is tied on.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
phrases.notes: A תנא quoted from the משנה in מקואות.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁל צֶמֶר וְשֶׁל שֵׂעָר אֵין חוֹצְצִין,
phrases.english: those (strings) of wool and of hair do not interpose,
phrases.notes: Disagrees with the first opinion of the משנה about wool.

phrases.english: because the water enters through them.
phrases.notes: The reason is that these materials absorb water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the same משנה, moving from the neck-strap to רבי יהודה's view on wool and hair strings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wool and hair strings are not a חציצה, because water passes through them.

steps.title: שמואל rules like רבי יהודה only for hair strings
steps.stepSummary: Through a chain of names, שמואל rules that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה only for strings of hair. This implies the הלכה does not follow him for wool.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said in the name of רב יהודה, who said in the name of שמואל: the הלכה follows רבי יהודה regarding hair strings.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא gives a practical ruling on רבי יהודה's view, and accepts only half of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה spoke about both wool and hair. שמואל says the הלכה follows him only for hair. So for wool, the הלכה follows the first opinion, and wool strings do block.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows (a certain opinion)
Strings or strands of hair

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the names. רַב יְהוּדָה here is an אמורא, a student of שמואל, who passes on the ruling. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה is the תנא from the משנה whose opinion is being ruled on.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical ruling: hair strings do not block, but wool strings do.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said that Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
phrases.notes: Each one heard it from the one before. This רב יהודה is an אמורא, not the תנא רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: The halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda regarding strings of hair.
phrases.notes: Only hair is mentioned, so the ruling does not cover wool.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a practical ruling on רבי יהודה's opinion from the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה that hair strings are not a חציצה. By implication, wool strings are.

steps.title: אביי asks: a הלכה ruling implies a dispute, but who disagrees about hair?
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges שמואל's wording. Saying 'the הלכה follows' implies someone disagrees, yet the משנה shows no one saying hair strings block.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: You say 'the הלכה follows him.' That implies others disagree!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי questions שמואל's ruling. Step 6 answers this challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We only need to say 'the הלכה follows X' when other opinions exist. In the משנה, the first opinion lists wool and linen strings as blocking, but says nothing about hair. So it seems no one disagrees with רבי יהודה about hair, which would make שמואל's ruling unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: By implication / it follows that
That they disagree

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not denying that hair strings do not block. He is only asking why שמואל used the words 'הלכה כ־', which suggest a real dispute.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
phrases.notes: Introduces the challenge to רב יוסף's report.

phrases.english: 'The halakha (follows him)' — this implies that they (the Rabbis) disagree!
phrases.notes: Rhetorical exclamation. The challenge is: where is the disagreement?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of שמואל's ruling in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling 'הלכה כרבי יהודה בחוטי שער'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The phrase 'הלכה כ־' is used only when there is a dispute. The משנה's first opinion does not mention hair, so there seems to be no one arguing with רבי יהודה about hair.

steps.title: Blocking a possible defense of שמואל's wording
steps.stepSummary: אביי imagines someone defending שמואל by saying רבי יהודה only mentioned hair because the תנא קמא disagreed about it. He rejects this: רבי יהודה may have said 'just as you agree with me on hair, agree with me on wool.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: if רבי יהודה had not heard the תנא קמא talking about hair strings, he would not have mentioned them either. But maybe he was saying 'just as' to them: just as you agree with me about hair strings, agree with me about wool strings too.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי is still pushing his challenge from step 4. He sees a possible way to save שמואל's wording and knocks it down before anyone can use it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The defense says that רבי יהודה naming hair proves someone forbade hair, so there is a real argument. אביי answers that naming hair does not prove an argument. רבי יהודה could be using the agreed case of hair to persuade the חכמים about wool. So 'the הלכה follows רבי יהודה on hair' still sounds wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you say (introduces a possible argument)
The first, unnamed opinion in a משנה
But perhaps (offers another possible reading)
Just as (a comparison used to persuade)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the 'וכי תימא' is the גמרא's real answer. It is a possible defense, and אביי rejects it right away with 'ודילמא.' The challenge to שמואל still stands.

phrases.english: And if you say,
had he not heard the first tanna
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: speaking about strings of hair,
he too would not have spoken about them —
phrases.notes: So this would suggest the תנא קמא forbade hair.

phrases.english: but perhaps he was saying 'just as' to them:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֵיכִי דְּמוֹדִיתוּ לִי בְּחוּטֵי שֵׂעָר,
phrases.english: just as you agree with me about strings of hair,
agree with me also about strings of wool.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא, אִי לָאו דְּשָׁמְעֵיהּ לְתַנָּא קַמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues אביי's challenge by closing off a possible defense of שמואל.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The possible proof that the תנא קמא forbade hair strings.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Mentioning hair does not prove a dispute. It can be a 'just as' argument built on an agreed case.

steps.title: The corrected version of שמואל's ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a version of שמואל's statement that avoids the problem: the חכמים agree with רבי יהודה about hair strings.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל: The חכמים agree with רבי יהודה about strings of hair.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers אביי's challenge by quoting שמואל with different wording. The new wording says there is no argument about hair at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי objected that 'the הלכה follows' implies a dispute that does not exist. This version says 'the חכמים agree,' which means everyone holds hair strings are not a חציצה. The argument is only about wool.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages agree

steps.whyThisMatters: It changes the picture from 'the הלכה goes like one side' to 'there is no dispute on hair,' which is exactly what אביי argued.

phrases.aramaic: אִיתְּמַר, אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: It was stated: Rav Naḥman said that Shmuel said:
The Sages agree with Rabbi Yehuda
about strings of hair.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר, אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge with a corrected version of שמואל's words.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל said 'the הלכה follows רבי יהודה' on hair, implying a dispute.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל said 'the חכמים agree with רבי יהודה' on hair. There is no dispute about hair.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the corrected version
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that the תנא קמא says wool strings block and hair strings do not, while רבי יהודה says neither blocks.
steps.simpleTranslation: This was also taught in a ברייתא: Strings of wool are a חציצה. Strings of hair are not a חציצה. רבי יהודה says: neither wool nor hair is a חציצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as support. It shows clearly that the argument is only about wool.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this ברייתא, the תנא קמא openly says hair strings are not a חציצה. So both sides agree on hair, exactly as the corrected version of שמואל says.

keyTerms.meaning: This was also taught in a ברייתא (brings support)
They block the water (are a חציצה)

phrases.english: It was also taught so:
Strings of wool block,
strings of hair do not block.
Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁל צֶמֶר וְשֶׁל שֵׂעָר אֵין חוֹצְצִין.
phrases.english: those of wool and those of hair do not block.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the corrected version of שמואל from step 6.
steps.raayaObject: That the חכמים agree hair strings are not a חציצה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where the תנא קמא explicitly says hair strings do not block.

steps.title: Our משנה also fits this view
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק shows that our משנה, which allows going out with hair strings but not wool, must be the חכמים. So the חכמים agree about hair.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Our משנה is also precise this way. It teaches: a woman may go out with strings of hair, whether from her own hair or from her friend's. Whose view is this? If you say רבי יהודה, then even wool strings should be allowed! So it must be the חכמים, and we learn from this that they do not argue about hair strings.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק brings another proof, this time from the משנה in our own פרק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allows only hair strings, not wool. רבי יהודה would allow wool too, so the משנה cannot be his view. It must be the חכמים, which shows they also allow hair strings.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה is also precise this way (its wording supports the point)
Whose view is this?
If you say (suggests an option to reject it)
Rather, is it not (introduces the only remaining option)

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
Our mishna is also precise this way,
as it teaches: A woman may go out with strings of hair,
whether from her own or from her friend's.
Whose view is it? If you say Rabbi Yehuda —
then even strings of wool too!
phrases.notes: רבי יהודה allows wool, so the משנה would have allowed it.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not the Rabbis,

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ בְּחוּטֵי שֵׂעָר לָא פְּלִיגִי.
phrases.english: and learn from this that about strings of hair they do not disagree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second proof, from our own משנה, to the ברייתא of step 7.
steps.raayaObject: That the חכמים agree hair strings are not a חציצה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Our משנה permits hair strings only, so it must be the חכמים and not רבי יהודה.

steps.title: The proof is accepted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the proof: the חכמים do not argue about hair strings.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts רב נחמן בר יצחק's proof and closes the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'שמע מינה' mean the proof stands. Both the ברייתא and our משנה confirm that everyone agrees hair strings are not a חציצה.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this (the proof is accepted)

steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees strings of hair are not a חציצה, so a woman may go out with them on שבת. The only argument is about wool: the חכמים say wool blocks, and רבי יהודה says it does not.

phrases.english: Learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the proof from step 8.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The חכמים agree with רבי יהודה that hair strings are not a חציצה. They argue only about wool.

steps.title: What is the טוטפת in the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the words 'not with a טוטפת' from the משנה and asks what a טוטפת is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said a woman may not go out with a 'totefet.' What is a 'totefet'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new item in the משנה's list and asks what the word טוטפת means. This sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before we can understand why the משנה forbids it, we need to know what the object is. The answer will decide whether the item is jewelry or something else, and that affects the הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: An item a woman wore on her head. Its exact identity is being discussed here.
What is? (Aramaic question word)

phrases.english: [The Mishnah said a woman may go out] not with a 'totefet.'
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting a phrase from the משנה.

phrases.english: What is a 'totefet'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the hair-string discussion, which ended in step 9, and moves to the next item in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What object is the טוטפת mentioned in the משנה?

steps.title: רב יוסף says it is a spice packet
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says a טוטפת is a packet of spices worn to protect against the evil eye.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: it is a small packet of spices.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives the first answer: a טוטפת is a little bag of spices worn for protection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By this explanation, the טוטפת is not jewelry. It is something worn for its protective power against עין הרע. That detail is exactly what אביי will attack next.

keyTerms.meaning: A small packet or bundle
Spices (according to the common explanation, used against the evil eye)

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
A packet of spices.
phrases.notes: It was worn to protect against the evil eye.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A טוטפת is a packet of spices worn for protection.

steps.title: אביי objects: it should be allowed like a proven amulet
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב יוסף: if the packet protects, it is like a proven קמיע, which is permitted on שבת. So why would the משנה forbid it?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Let it be like a proven amulet, and it should be permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רב יוסף's explanation. A protective packet should count like a proven amulet, and that is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קמיע מומחה, an amulet that has been shown to work, may be worn out on שבת. It counts as something worn on the body, not as carrying. If the טוטפת is a protective spice packet, it should get the same law. But the משנה forbids the טוטפת, so רב יוסף's explanation cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: A proven amulet, one shown to be effective. It is allowed to be worn out on שבת.
And it should be permitted

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Let it be like a proven amulet,
and it should be permitted!
phrases.notes: Yet the משנה forbids the totefet.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי תִּהְוֵי כְּקָמֵיעַ מוּמְחֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's identification from step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that a טוטפת is a protective spice packet.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A protective item works like a proven קמיע, which is permitted. That clashes with the משנה forbidding the טוטפת.

steps.title: רב יהודה in the name of אביי: it is a forehead ornament
steps.stepSummary: Because of the objection, רב יהודה quotes אביי: a טוטפת is אפוזייני, a forehead ornament.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב יהודה said in the name of אביי: it is an אפוזייני, a forehead ornament.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops רב יוסף's answer and gives a new one. The טוטפת is a piece of jewelry worn across the forehead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא shows that the earlier explanation is rejected. As jewelry, the טוטפת fits the reason the משנה forbids ornaments: a woman might take it off to show a friend and then carry it four אמות in the public domain.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; signals that the earlier answer is rejected
A forehead ornament or band
In the name of

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Yehuda said in the name of Abaye:
An appuzainei (a forehead ornament).

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּאַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב יוסף's rejected explanation with a new one that avoids אביי's objection.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The טוטפת is a protective spice packet.
steps.terutzMaskana: The טוטפת is a forehead ornament, so it falls under the ornaments the משנה forbids.

steps.title: A ברייתא lists the טוטפת among ornaments
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports the view that the טוטפת is an ornament. It lists the טוטפת together with a gilded hairnet and the סרביטין fastened to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא: A woman may go out with a gold-plated hairnet, and with a טוטפת and סרביטין that are fastened to it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up רב יהודה's answer. The טוטפת appears there in a list of head jewelry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the ברייתא groups the טוטפת with the hairnet and other ornaments, it shows that the טוטפת is jewelry, not a spice packet. In the ברייתא it is permitted only because it is fastened to the hairnet. A woman will not take off her head covering in the street to show it, so there is no fear she will carry it.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא also teaches this; introduces support
A hairnet
Ornaments hanging from the hairnet
That are fastened (attached)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the ברייתא contradicts the משנה. The משנה forbids a loose טוטפת. The ברייתא permits one fastened to the hairnet, which she won't remove to show off.

phrases.english: It was also taught this way [in a baraita]:
A woman may go out with a gilded hairnet,
and with a totefet and with sarvitin
that are fastened to it.
phrases.notes: Fastened to the hairnet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the identification given in step 13.
steps.raayaObject: That the טוטפת is a head ornament (אפוזייני).
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא listing the טוטפת among ornaments fastened to a gilded hairnet.

steps.title: Which one is the טוטפת and which are the סרביטין?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how to tell apart the two ornaments named in the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which is the טוטפת, and which are the סרביטין?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the exact difference between the two head ornaments. This sets up רבי אבהו's definitions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both items hang from the hairnet, so it is unclear how they differ. The question asks for a precise description of each one.

keyTerms.meaning: Which one?

phrases.english: Which is a totefet and which are sarvitin?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of terms from the ברייתא in step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The physical difference between a טוטפת and סרביטין.

steps.title: רבי אבהו defines the two ornaments
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו says the טוטפת goes around the forehead from ear to ear, and the סרביטין hang down to the cheeks.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: The טוטפת is the band that goes around her from ear to ear. The סרביטין are the pieces that reach down to her cheeks.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו describes each ornament. The טוטפת is a band across the forehead, and the סרביטין hang down the sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This confirms that the טוטפת is a forehead band, matching רב יהודה's explanation of אפוזייני. The סרביטין are separate hanging pieces that reach the cheeks.

keyTerms.meaning: That goes around
From ear to ear
Her cheeks

steps.whatToRemember: The טוטפת is not a protective spice packet, since that would be permitted like a proven קמיע. It is a forehead band of jewelry going from ear to ear. The סרביטין are ornaments hanging down to the cheeks.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
Totefet is that which goes around her from ear to ear.
Sarvitin are those that reach down to her cheeks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A טוטפת is a forehead band from ear to ear. סרביטין hang down to the cheeks.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The טוטפת of the משנה is a forehead ornament, which confirms רב יהודה in the name of אביי.

steps.title: Poor women and rich women make these ornaments differently
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says poor women make the טוטפת and סרביטין from colored materials, and rich women make them from silver and gold.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: Poor women make them out of different kinds of colored materials. Wealthy women make them out of silver and gold.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא adds one more fact about the two ornaments that were just defined, the טוטפת and the סרביטין. He tells us what they are made of.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 told us where each ornament sits on the head. Now רב הונא tells us what it is made of. Each woman makes it according to what she can afford. This confirms that these are real jewelry-type ornaments, which fits אביי's explanation that a טוטפת is an ornament.

keyTerms.meaning: Poor women
Wealthy women
Different kinds of colored materials
Silver and gold

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
Poor women make them
phrases.notes: "Them" means the טוטפת and סרביטין just discussed.

phrases.english: from different kinds of colored materials;
wealthy women make them
of silver and of gold.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: עֲנִיּוֹת עוֹשִׂין אוֹתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds information about the materials of the ornaments defined in Step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The טוטפת and סרביטין are made of colored materials by poor women and of silver and gold by wealthy women.

steps.title: רבי ינאי is unsure what a כבול is
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next item in the משנה, כבול. רבי ינאי asks whether it means a slave's seal, so that a wool cap would be allowed, or a wool cap, so that a slave's seal would surely be forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says a woman may not go out with a כבול. רבי ינאי said: I do not know what this כבול is. Maybe the משנה means a slave's seal, and a woolen cap is fine. Or maybe the משנה means a woolen cap, and a slave's seal is forbidden all the more so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next word in the משנה, כבול. רבי ינאי admits he does not know what it means and lays out two possible readings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two readings lead to different practical rulings. If כבול means a slave's seal, only that is forbidden, and a woman's wool cap is permitted. If כבול means a wool cap, then the wool cap is forbidden. A slave's seal would then be forbidden even more, because it is an even stronger case.

keyTerms.meaning: An item in the משנה that a woman may not go out with; its meaning is unclear
A slave's seal, a mark that shows someone is a slave
A woolen cap worn on the hair
It is fine, it is permitted
All the more so

steps.confusionAlert: רבי ינאי is not arguing with anyone. He is honestly unsure what the word means. The "all the more so" in the second option means only this: if even a wool cap is forbidden, then a slave's seal is surely forbidden too.

phrases.english: "And not with a kavul."
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה, the heading for this new discussion.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yannai said:
This kavul, I do not know what it is.
Is it a slave's seal that we learned about?

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל כִּיפָּה שֶׁל צֶמֶר שַׁפִּיר דָּמֵי,
phrases.english: If so, a woolen cap would be fine.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא כִּיפָּה שֶׁל צֶמֶר תְּנַן —
phrases.english: Or perhaps it is a woolen cap that we learned about?
If so, a slave's seal would be forbidden all the more so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the טוטפת discussion and opens a new discussion about the next item in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the כבול in the משנה is a slave's seal or a woman's woolen cap.

steps.title: רבי אבהו says כבול most likely means a wool cap
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו says it makes more sense that the משנה is talking about a woolen cap.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: It is more reasonable to follow the view that the משנה is talking about a woolen cap.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers רבי ינאי's question. He picks the second option: the כבול is a woman's woolen cap.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו chooses one of the two options. This means a woolen cap is forbidden in the street on שבת, and a slave's seal surely is too. The next step brings a ברייתא to back him up.

keyTerms.meaning: It is reasonable, it makes sense
Like the one who says

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
It is reasonable to follow the one who says
that we learned about a woolen cap.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in Step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The כבול in the משנה is a woman's woolen cap.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows the כבול is a cap worn under the hairnet
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא allows a woman to wear a כבול and an איסטמא into a courtyard. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר allows the כבול even in the public domain, because anything worn under the hairnet may be worn outside. This fits a wool cap, not a slave's seal.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this: A woman may go out with a כבול and with an איסטמא into the courtyard. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: even with a כבול into the public domain. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר stated a rule: anything worn under the hairnet, a woman may go out with it. Anything worn over the hairnet, she may not go out with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support רבי אבהו's view that the כבול is a woman's wool cap.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר explains why the כבול may be worn: it sits under the hairnet. A woman will not uncover her hair in public to show it off, so there is no worry that she will take it off and carry it. Something worn under a woman's hairnet is clearly a cap for the hair, not a slave's seal. This supports רבי אבהו.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא also teaches this, a supporting source
Another head item mentioned in the ברייתא; it is explained in the next steps
Courtyard, a semi-private area
The public domain
Hairnet
A general rule

steps.whyThisMatters: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר gives a clear practical test for head coverings on שבת. What is under the hairnet may be worn outside. What is over it may not, because she might take it off to show it and end up carrying it.

phrases.english: And it was also taught this way in a baraita:
A woman may go out with a kavul
and with an istema into the courtyard.
Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
Even with a kavul into the public domain.

phrases.aramaic: כְּלָל אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar stated a general rule:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל שֶׁהוּא לְמַטָּה מִן הַשְּׂבָכָה — יוֹצְאִין בּוֹ,
phrases.english: Anything worn beneath the hairnet, one may go out with it.
phrases.notes: She will not uncover her hair in public, so she will not take it off to show it.

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל שֶׁהוּא לְמַעְלָה מִן הַשְּׂבָכָה — אֵין יוֹצְאִין בּוֹ.
phrases.english: Anything worn above the hairnet, one may not go out with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to support רבי אבהו's answer in Step 19.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אבהו's view that the כבול is a woman's woolen cap.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's rule about items worn under or over the hairnet.

steps.title: What is an איסטמא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the איסטמא mentioned in the ברייתא is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is an איסטמא?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא used an unfamiliar word, איסטמא. The גמרא stops to ask what it means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a simple question about a word. It opens a short side discussion about the meaning of an item in the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: What is

phrases.english: What is an "istema"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a word that appeared in the ברייתא in Step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word איסטמא.

steps.title: רבי אבהו explains איסטמא as ביזיוני
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו says an איסטמא is a ביזיוני.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: It is a ביזיוני.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers that איסטמא means ביזיוני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו lived in ארץ ישראל, and ביזיוני is a word from the Aramaic spoken there. The scholars in בבל did not know this word. So the answer itself needs explaining, which leads to the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: A word from the Aramaic of ארץ ישראל, used to explain איסטמא

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
"Beizyunei."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 21, but with a word that will itself need explaining.

steps.title: What is ביזיוני?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי אבהו's word ביזיוני means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a ביזיוני?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו's explanation used a word the people in בבל did not know. Now the גמרא asks what that word means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the explanation needs its own explanation. The גמרא wants a definition everyone can understand.

phrases.english: What is "beizyunei"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the unfamiliar word used in Step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word ביזיוני.

steps.title: It is a band that gathers in loose hairs
steps.stepSummary: אביי, quoting רב, explains that it is a כליא פרוחי, something that holds in stray hairs.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said in the name of רב: It is something that gathers in hairs that stick out.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי, quoting רב, gives the final, clear definition. The איסטמא, or ביזיוני, is a small cap or band that holds in loose hairs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ends the chain of definitions: איסטמא means ביזיוני, which means כליא פרוחי. It is a small cap or ribbon that keeps stray hairs from sticking out of the head covering. That is why the ברייתא lists it together with the כבול as a head item a woman may wear in the courtyard.

keyTerms.meaning: Something that gathers in hairs that stick out, a small cap or ribbon

steps.whatToRemember: The כבול in the משנה is a woman's woolen cap (רבי אבהו, supported by the ברייתא). רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's rule: what is worn under the hairnet may be worn outside on שבת, and what is worn over it may not. An איסטמא is a small band that holds in stray hairs.

phrases.english: Abaye said that Rav said:
Something that gathers in protruding hairs.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי אָמַר רַב: כָּלְיָא פָּרוֹחֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 23 and completes the definition of איסטמא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ביזיוני is a small cap or band that gathers in hairs sticking out of the head covering.

steps.title: Three rules about the felt hair-covering
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches three rules about the אִיסְטְמָא. כלאים does not apply to it, it does not become impure through נגעים, and women may not go out with it to the רשות הרבים on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Three things were said about an אִיסְטְמָא. The prohibition of כלאים does not apply to it. It does not become impure with צרעת. Women may not go out with it into the public domain.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know what an אִיסְטְמָא is, the גמרא brings a ברייתא that lists three הלכות about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אִיסְטְמָא is made of pressed felt and is not woven. That is why כלאים, the ban on mixing wool and linen, does not apply to it, and why it cannot get the impurity of נגעים, which applies only to woven garments. The third rule fits the earlier ברייתא from step 20: a woman may wear it in a courtyard, but not out in the רשות הרבים.

keyTerms.meaning: A felt band or cap that holds in a woman's stray hairs
The forbidden mixture of wool and linen (שעטנז)
The impurity of צרעת, which can affect garments
The public domain, where carrying on שבת is forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: "אין בה משום כלאים" does NOT mean the אִיסְטְמָא never has wool and linen in it. It means that even if it does, the prohibition does not apply, because felt is not woven.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the legal status of a garment can depend on how it was made. Pressed felt is treated differently from woven cloth for both כלאים and טומאת נגעים.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן, שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים נֶאֶמְרוּ בְּאִיסְטָמָא:
phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: three things were said regarding an istema:
phrases.notes: A ברייתא, a teaching from the era of the משנה that was not included in the משנה.

phrases.english: there is no prohibition of diverse kinds (wool and linen) in it,
phrases.notes: Felt is pressed, not woven, so כלאים does not apply.

phrases.english: and it does not become impure with leprosy,
phrases.notes: Only woven garments can become impure through נגעים.

phrases.english: and one may not go out with it to the public domain.
phrases.notes: This refers to שבת. It matches the earlier ברייתא, which allowed it only in a courtyard.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן, שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים נֶאֶמְרוּ בְּאִיסְטָמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defining the item in steps 21 to 24, the גמרא brings a ברייתא listing its halachic status.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The אִיסְטְמָא is exempt from כלאים, is not susceptible to נגעים, and may not be worn into the רשות הרבים on שבת.

steps.title: רבי שמעון begins to add another rule
steps.stepSummary: In the name of רבי שמעון, the Sages begin to add one more point to this ברייתא. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the name of רבי שמעון they said: Also...
steps.whatsHappening: This line is a setup. The ברייתא starts quoting רבי שמעון, who is about to add another rule, and the rest of the sentence comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "אַף" ("also") tells us that רבי שמעון is extending what was just said. We will only learn what he adds when the text continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: "In the name of": quoting a teaching from a specific Sage
"Also" or "even": signals an addition to what was just said

phrases.english: In the name of Rabbi Shimon they said: also,
phrases.notes: The statement is cut off here and continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It extends the ברייתא in step 25 by beginning an additional rule in רבי שמעון's name.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון adds a further rule about the אִיסְטְמָא. Its content continues on the next amud.
